      "frozenFields": {
        "kind": "bug",
        "title": "A cancelled blueprint operation whose work-item no worker has applied can never settle: cancel only marks it, and every other writer is refused",
        "summary": "Observed 2026-10-06 14:30-14:45Z (su-7f8d7809, plan crm-agent-sales-onboarding-apps-2026-10-06 P-010). The live E2E submitted crm onboarding-step (receipt 38) creating WI-10006707 (harness crm, kind crm-proposal, unassigned), then cancelled it through the seam: cancelBlueprintOperation (packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-service.ts ~L680) returned accepted:true, handled:false, effected:false and only stamped payload.blueprintCancellation. 15 minutes later the item is still open. Placement skips it (coord-program-workflow excludes blueprintCancellation; operation-worker-binding requireUncancelled), so no worker will ever take it, and a direct work_items:set_state dropped through the app invoker is refused: \"blueprint operation effect refused: accepted operation item requires its applied worker\". Result: every cancel before a worker applies leaves a permanent open, unplaceable item and an operation stuck in cancelling. Proposed fix: when cancel finds no applied worker binding on an unsettled item, settle it to a cancelled/dropped terminal state inside the same transaction (the operator is the authority when no executor exists); add a test that cancel-before-apply reaches phase terminal / outcome cancelled. Live example left in place: WI-10006707. Evidence: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/p010/e2e-2.log, drop-3.log."
      },
      "frozenUpdatedAt": "2026-10-10T15:08:11.056Z",

      "frozenFields": {
        "kind": "bug",
        "title": "Shared result-door scratch persistence stalls or fails before overflow output becomes recoverable",
        "summary": "Different handlers reach the same post-handler result-door scratch writer, then report spill-write-failed/output_spill_failed, commonly ETIMEDOUT after 30000ms. Coordination threads (EI-25424920546318879), document reads (EI-25425159282204609), and transcript tails (EI-25425669800696149) lose overflow without a recoverable cursor. Capture and send mutations retain committed receipts but lose remaining output (EI-25423907483948308, EI-25424167976820667).         "summary": "Observed 2026-10-27 on consult conv-mvq2x83t-0000-2212927f6ee640f8aa2857b0a5181c49 (requester su-4aab087c, origin EI-25940249793936216, cascade flavor decision-review).\n\nTimeline (harness_shared.consult_state + the answering session's own transcript):\n- 02:41:13Z consult created by consult:get_feedback (set_blocker decision-review cascade).\n- 02:43:37Z dispatch: full Claude/fable session launched as su-4d187f6c-066b-4679-9e6a-78c0535cb5fa ('convert' of su-ac5c6b74's transcript), host registered after 126ms.\n- 02:50:49Z requester closed the consult `cant_help` with reason \"created accidentally by classifying the fleet leader's D-334 route dependency as a product-owner decision\".\n- ~02:56Z the answering session, having read the thread, plan_decisions, two work-items and the source transcript (~13 minutes of work), called consult:reply and was refused `consult_not_open` (state closed_cant_help). No signal of the closure reached it in between: no coord inject, no wake, no [coord+N] line.\n\nDefect: closing (or declining/expiring) a consult does not cancel or notify the in-flight dispatched answerer. The answering session only learns on its terminal write, after the full research cost has been paid. consult_state.dispatch_attempts records answeringOwnerId, so the recipient is known.\n\nProposed fix: in consult:close (and the decline/expiry paths) when dispatch_attempts has a dispatched answeringOwnerId whose session is live, (a) mark the dispatch cancelled in consult_state and (b) coord:send that owner a stand-down with wake:'required' (summary 'consult <id> closed <state> — stop; do not reply') so the next tool round surfaces it as a [coord+N] line. Optionally the answering session's launch brief should carry an `events:await consult:closed:<conversation_id>` key so the harness can inject the closure mid-turn. Recurrence guard: a test that closes a consult with a live dispatched answerer and asserts the stand-down message exists in coord for that ownerId.\n\nSeparate, smaller signal (not a second record): the requester's reason says the consult was auto-created from a set_blocker product-decision cascade for what was a fleet-leader routing question — the cascade had no 'this is a fleet-leader question, route to @fleet-leader:<slug>' branch, so a full external answerer was spent on it."

        "title": "scorecards:get per-criterion reads too slow to page a 9-criterion card inside one code:run (55s nested timeout)",
        "summary": "Observed 2026-10-13 ~21:16Z during grading-integrity audit of EI-25900285445623116 (build 78cd58273a, :3070). A code:run looping scorecards:get {issueId, criterionKey, evidenceOffset:0} over 6 criterion keys (each evidence <=1086 chars, complete in one page) failed with `request_timeout: nested tool \"code:run\" exceeded 55000ms via tools:invoke`. That implies more than 9s per small per-criterion read. The grading-integrity brief and card both require reading every criterion's evidence through this paged per-criterion door. Auditors therefore cannot batch it in code:run as the playbook recommends. They fall back to N parallel direct calls, and those then trip the aggregate output budget: 7 of 12 parallel calls spilled to scratch with 'aggregate-output-budget-exceeded', so each needed extra capability:read turns. Cause UNKNOWN / unconfirmed: possibly each criterionKey read recomputes the full card (currentness, evidenceBindingCurrentness, auditTarget) per call. The box also reported 'Perf budget breached (ambient)' at the time, so load correlation is possible; that is still a bug per the responsiveness design. Suggested fix: one call returning all criteria's complete evidence when it fits a size bound (e.g. criterionKeys:[...] or evidence:'all'), and/or cache the per-card currentness computation across criterion pages. Repro: code:run { script: for 6 keys await tools.scorecards.get({issueId:'EI-25900285445623116', criterionKey:k, evidenceOffset:0}) }."

Suggested fix: the watchdog should skip sessions under its idle threshold, and the carry should re-inject the original kickoff (or refuse to resume a role-scoped session whose kickoff is missing)."
